newsitem.title: HONG KONG: S&P warns HK, China investors to keep clear heads.
newsitem.headline: S&P warns HK, China investors to keep clear heads.

text.p: Standard and Poor's Corp on Wednesday warned investors and lenders to maintain perspective about commercial risks in China and Hong Kong amid the optimism surrounding the territory's handover to Chinese rule.

"The closer union of a high-income, international financial center with the world's emerging economic giant has relatively little commerical downside," Paul Coughlin, managing director of S&P's Hong Kong office, said in a statement.
Nevertheless, Coughlin said, investors should not be lulled into "a false sense of security." As anywhere else, Hong Kong and China are susceptible to cycles in property and equity markets, he said.
Hong Kong reverts to China at midnight on June 30 after more than 150 years of British colonial rule.

S&P cited Hong Kong's extraordinary level of property prices, the high cost of maintaining corporate operations, and the lack of operating histories or unimpressive cash flows of some China-related companies as reasons why investors should pay particular attention to credit quality in China and Hong Kong.
"Despite rapid economic growth in this region, there is no guarantee of universal commercial success," Coughlin said.
In May, S&P upgraded the ratings of both Hong Kong and China. It assesses the foreign currency obligations of Hong Kong at A-plus and of China at BBB-plus.
